title: Origen Writes on Demonic Hierarchy and Powers
description: Origen of Alexandria (~185-253 CE) developed an influential Christian demonological framework in his major works, particularly Contra Celsum (c. 248 CE) and De Principiis, arguing for a hierarchical demonic order under Satan's command capable of tempting and misleading humans. Origen accepted the reality of demonic intervention in human affairs while arguing that Christian faith and practice provided the means to resist demonic power. His elaborate angelology and demonology, influenced by Platonic and Jewish traditions, provided the Christian intellectual framework that would later be developed by Jerome, Augustine, and ultimately the scholastics into the mature demonological tradition underlying witch prosecution.
historiographical_note: Stuart Clark's Thinking with Demons extensively analyzes how patristic demonology including Origen's contributions constituted the intellectual foundation for later early modern demonological treatises, demonstrating doctrinal continuity across fifteen centuries.
source_method: Published scholarship; Origen Contra Celsum; De Principiis; Clark, Thinking with Demons (1997)
